newsitem.title: USA: Missouri wheat free of Karnal bunt - survey.
newsitem.headline: Missouri wheat free of Karnal bunt - survey.

text.p: Wheat grown in Missouri was certified to be free of the Karnal bunt fungus, the state's department of agriculture said.
A survey conducted by the federal and state departments of agriculture showed that almost 700 samples taken from 69 Missouri counties tested negative for the fungus.

"These survey reults enble us to show other countries that our grain shipments do not carry Karnal bunt and that the disease is not present in Missouri nor widespread in the United States," Mike Brown, state entomologist for the Missouri Department of Agriculture, said in a statement.

Karnal bunt was first detected in the United States in Arizona wheat crops last March. Although the disease is not a threat to humans or animals if consumed, it causes infected plants to produce less grain and the grain quality is poor.
In 1995, Missouri produced 48 million bushels of winter wheat valued at $185 million.
